title: SouthPoint Retail renewal & capacity uplift: EU edge onboarding + pricing review
next_steps: Send revised tiered pricing spreadsheet with committed throughput tiers (Maya) by 2027-08-16
Share SOC2 + EU data residency checklist and KMS integrations doc (Carlos) by 2027-08-18
Schedule 2-day benchmarking window for EU edge with SouthPoint test set (Carlos & Tom) week of 2027-08-23
Follow up call to review benchmark results and finalize contract amendment (Maya) on 2027-08-27
action_items: Carlos - run throughput baseline and 95th percentile latency runs on g5x2+quantized model variant using SouthPoint test corpus by 2027-08-20
Maya - prepare committed capacity pricing table and three options for burst vs reserved by 2027-08-16
Tom - share current traffic profile & 90-day seq length distribution CSV (anonymized) by 2027-08-15
Lara - indicate procurement preferred contract term (12/24/36 months) and billing cadence by 2027-08-19
header:
Date: 2027-08-14 | Time: 09:32-10:20 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Anya Feldman (Redwood CSM); Evelyn Cho, Tom Bennett, Lara Nguyen, Samir Das (SouthPoint)
summary: Check-in ahead of renewal to agree on capacity uplift for Q4, validate EU edge onboarding plan, and review tiered committed pricing. Customer wants an uplift of steady reserved capacity plus EU edge nodes and a short benchmarking window to validate latency SLAs. Questions around KMS, SOC2, and billing term options were discussed.
topics: Committed capacity tiers vs burst pricing
EU edge onboarding and data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick roll call then i'll pass it to carlos for the tech bits.
[00:10] Evelyn Cho: hi all, Evelyn here from SouthPoint. thanks.
[00:15] Tom Bennett: Tom - platform engineering.
[00:18] Lara Nguyen: Lara - procurement.
[00:20] Samir Das: Samir - SRE.
[00:22] Maya Patel: great. goal today: align on the capacity uplift you're asking for, confirm the eu edge onboarding plan and agree next steps on benchmarks + commercial.  should be a short sync.
[00:36] Carlos Rivera: yeah hi, real quick, i pulled together a config suggestion based on the usage Tom sent last week. looks like your 95th pctl latency target is sub 180ms for the 1-2k tps baseline, and you wanted EU edge for legal/regulatory routing, correct?
[00:52] Tom Bennett: correct. main constraint is peak events during promos - short spiky traffic, that's where burst capacity matters. for steady state we want reserved so cost predictable.
[01:05] Evelyn Cho: and from ml side, we also want to ensure KV cache warmup doesn't add tails during afternoon spike windows. we've seen that with another provider.
[01:15] Carlos Rivera: understood. recommendation: a two-tier pool - reserved baseline (g5x2-equivalent nodes, quantized model) + burst pool for peak. for EU edge we'd provision dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 with private control plane, which maps to our Redwood Private offering, or you can use limited Dedicated with VPC peering depending on how much isolation you need.
[01:40] Samir Das: can you clarify the difference between private and dedicated here? last time the names got mixed up in our notes - which one gives us full customer-managed VPC?
[01:49] Carlos Rivera: sure, sorry — Redwood Private is the customer-managed control plane with VPC and KMS integrations; Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity managed by Redwood but isolated at tenant level. Private is for full network control and on-prem-like constraints. apologies if i said the product names funky earlier.
[02:10] Lara Nguyen: procurement question — what's the minimum commitment term for pricing tiers? we prefer 12 or 24 months but need to see cost delta for 36.
[02:20] Maya Patel: i'll put together three term options and pricing spreads. we can show committed throughput bands and optional burst credit buckets.
[02:30] Tom Bennett: for the benchmarking, can we run a 48-hour window against eu-edge with a replay of our June promo traffic? we need to see tail latency under load and validate cache hit improvements.
[02:41] Carlos Rivera: absolutely. propose we run baseline + two elevated runs: baseline steady, burst replay, and one with cold caches. we'll instrument prefix/KV cache metrics and token-level latency.
[02:55] Evelyn Cho: and can you measure quantized vs fp16 to show any quality diffs? we want to surface hallucination/regression risk too.
[03:05] Carlos Rivera: yes, we'll include perf + basic output-stat comparisons. caveat: evals here are lightweight, not a full rerun of your human evals, but enough to flag big shifts.
[03:18] Maya Patel: Lara, timeline on legal/PO? if procurement holds a month, we need to know to align committed start date.
[03:27] Lara Nguyen: ideally we sign amendment before 2027-09-01. that's our target; finance needs price, SOW and security addendum to approve.
[03:36] Maya Patel: good note. we'll aim for that.
[03:40] Samir Das: security — you mentioned KMS, we use a customer-managed key. does Redwood support external KMS/HSM or only cloud-provider KMS?
[03:49] Carlos Rivera: we support AWS KMS and BYOK flows; we also have integrations for external HSM via our Private deploys but that's more involved. i'll share the KMS integration doc after the call.
[04:02] Evelyn Cho: do you have SOC2 + EU data residency details for the edge nodes? last vendor said the edge was only cache and control plane was still us-east. we need full residency guarantees.
[04:15] Anya Feldman: we can provide SOC2 Type II report and an EU residency checklist; for Private deployments we can pin data plane and control plane in eu region. i'll attach both.
[04:27] Tom Bennett: perfect. on capacity sizing, our 90-day seq length distribution is skewed — a lot of mid-length conversations. i'll send the anonymized CSV today.
[04:37] Carlos Rivera: that will help set batching and kernel selection. initial suggestion: reserve 12 g5x2-equivalent nodes for baseline with autoscale up to 30 nodes for burst via a separate burst pool. pricing examples in the sheet i'll send.
[04:55] Lara Nguyen: pricing concern — we saw a list price with fairly high peak costs. is there a way to soften burst by using credits or a smoothing window?
[05:06] Maya Patel: yes, we offer burst credits as an addon or you can purchase a higher reserved tier and cap autoscale — both reduce unit cost. i'll include a couple of blends in the spreadsheet.
[05:18] Evelyn Cho: on quality, if we quantize aggressively to save cost, what's the rollback plan if we see model regressions in prod?
[05:27] Carlos Rivera: rollback is straightforward — we keep model variants pinned per route; we can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to fp16 if quality drops. Redwood has eval hooks and you can set prompt-based regressions to trigger a rollback.
[05:42] Tom Bennett: latency SLO — you mentioned 95th pctl. can you guarantee 95th under burst? last vendor's guaranteed number was without cold-cache impacts.
[05:52] Carlos Rivera: we provide SLOs for reserved baseline; burst SLOs are best-effort unless you commit to a larger reserved tier. cold-cache tail is callout — that's why we're proposing a warm-up plan and prefix caching. in our Dedicated/Private configs we can keep warmed-up replicas for promo windows.
[06:10] Samir Das: operational question — logs and tracing. can we send audit logs to our SIEM?
[06:17] Anya Feldman: yes, audit logs and token-level cost traces can be exported to your S3 or Splunk via forwarder; RBAC is supported through SSO/SAML.
[06:29] Lara Nguyen: what about data retention? we need 2 year audit logs for compliance.
[06:35] Anya Feldman: retention policy is configurable; for Private we can retain as per your policy. for hosted tiers we have standard retention but we can negotiate longer retention as an add-on.
[06:48] Maya Patel: OK, quick recap so we're aligned: 1) SouthPoint wants reserved baseline + burst pool and EU edge nodes 2) Benchmark window to validate latency and cache behavior 3) Pricing options for 12/24/36 months + burst credits 4) Security docs (SOC2, KMS/HSM, residency) to be provided. any additions?
[07:06] Tom Bennett: can we also add a run that simulates cache warmup after a deploy? that was where we saw a regression previously.
[07:13] Carlos Rivera: yep will include a cold-to-warm sequence in the bench.
[07:18] Evelyn Cho: mic question — sorry quick one, on model quantization, will we have a human-in-the-loop flag to route flagged outputs to a higher-precision variant?
[07:27] Carlos Rivera: you can do route-by-score or by route config; we have function-calling style hooks and reroute rules to send flagged requests to a high-quality path.
[07:38] Lara Nguyen: procurement — if we sign a 24-month deal with a committed throughput, can you provide a revenue/procurement-friendly invoicing schedule? quarterly invoicing preferred.
[07:48] Maya Patel: yes, quarterly invoicing is fine; we'll present those options.
[07:53] Samir Das: any surprises we should know before proving the Private option? like lead time?
[07:58] Carlos Rivera: Private deployments typically have a 6-8 week lead time for region-specific network, certs, and HSM integrations; Dedicated can be faster, 2-3 weeks for standard regions. exact depends on legal approvals.
[08:12] Tom Bennett: do you have a runbook for incident responses and on-call handover for Private?
[08:20] Anya Feldman: yes, we'll share the SRE runbook and SLAs — we also provide a named SE escalation path during onboarding.
[08:30] Lara Nguyen: okay, procurement will need the SOW and a clean security addendum to avoid endless redlines.
[08:38] Maya Patel: noted. i'll push a draft SOW with the amendment language.
[08:43] Carlos Rivera: one more technical note — for the EU edge we'll ensure model weights and token logs don't leave eu-west region; control plane metadata can be in another region but we can pin it if needed in Private.
[09:00] Evelyn Cho: that's critical, thanks.
[09:03] Maya Patel: anything else from you all?
[09:07] Tom Bennett: no, that's it.
[09:10] Lara Nguyen: no.
[09:12] Samir Das: all good.
[09:14] Maya Patel: perfect. next steps as we listed: i'll send the pricing options and SOW draft; carlos will share benchmark plan and KMS doc; anya will attach SOC2 + runbooks. we'll meet after the benchmark week to finalize amendment. thanks everyone.
[09:30] Evelyn Cho: thanks.
[09:32] Tom Bennett: thanks all.
[09:33] call ended.
[47:30] (end of recording)
